summary:
**Earth Information Jukebox – Listen to a Changing Planet** is an interactive web application that transforms real-world Earth science data into sound, allowing people to experience our changing planet through both audio and visualisation.

We developed an interactive sonification platform using NASA and NOAA datasets, including NASA GISTEMP global temperature records, atmospheric CO₂ measurements from Mauna Loa, ocean surface temperatures, Arctic sea ice extent, vegetation indices and wildfire data. Using mathematical audio synthesis and the Web Audio API, the application translates scientific measurements into musical patterns and sounds. Users can explore datasets through playback, seeking, speed adjustments, pitch controls and interactive visualisations, including a digital globe and frequency spectrum visualiser. It also features a guided experience called "A Warming World".

The project addresses the challenge of making complex Earth science information more accessible, engaging and understandable. By turning environmental data into sound, it offers an alternative way to explore climate change and planetary processes, including for people who may find conventional charts difficult to interpret. Our goal is to make Earth science an experience that people can not only see, but hear.
details:
Project Details — Earth Information Jukebox: Listen to a Changing Planet

Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive scientific sonification platform that reimagines how humanity experiences planetary data. Instead of limiting Earth science to graphs, maps and numerical reports, we developed a system that translates environmental measurements into dynamic, mathematically generated sound. The central innovation is that scientific data does not simply accompany the experience; it becomes the source of the audio itself.

How It Works and What We Developed

We engineered a complete data-to-sound pipeline that extracts environmental measurements, validates and normalises them, applies mathematical scaling, maps them to musical frequencies and generates sound in real time. Users can explore how different environmental variables behave through an interactive listening experience.

The platform integrates multiple scientific datasets, including:

  • NASA GISTEMP v4: Global temperature anomalies and long-term warming patterns.
  • NOAA Mauna Loa: Atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements.
  • NOAA Ocean Surface Temperature: Changes in ocean temperatures.
  • NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice: Historical Arctic sea ice extent.
  • NASA MODIS: Vegetation indices (NDVI) and wildfire-related data.
  • NASA POWER API: Live-accessible environmental and meteorological measurements.

Our audio engine is built entirely around mathematical sound synthesis using the native Web Audio API. It does not depend on prerecorded music or audio samples. Environmental values are translated into frequencies, musical intervals, pitch progressions and other sound characteristics. We implemented multiple musical scales, including Major, Minor, Pentatonic, Blues, Chromatic, Whole Tone and Dorian, allowing scientific patterns to be experienced through different tonal structures.

The audio engine also incorporates oscillators, overtones, dynamic filters, amplitude envelopes, stereo panning, synthetic reverberation and frequency analysis. This creates a responsive sonic representation rather than simply playing a fixed soundtrack.

Interactive Visual and Audio Experience

We developed a custom procedural Earth globe using Canvas 2D, alongside an FFT-based audio spectrum and waveform visualiser operating at approximately 60 FPS. Custom SVG charts display the underlying scientific measurements, with interactive playhead scrubbing that connects the visual data directly to the listening experience.

Users can play, pause, stop, seek through datasets, adjust playback speed from 0.1× to 5×, and control volume. A guided experience, A Warming World, takes users through an exploration of long-term environmental changes.

This creates a connection between three dimensions of scientific understanding: the original measurement, its visual representation and its audible interpretation.

Technology and Engineering

The application was developed using:

  • Next.js 16 and React 19: Application architecture and interactive interface.
  • TypeScript 5: Strongly typed application and audio-engine logic.
  • Tailwind CSS 4: Responsive interface design.
  • Web Audio API: Mathematical and procedural audio synthesis.
  • Canvas 2D: Procedural Earth globe rendering.
  • Custom SVG: Scientific data visualisations and interactive charts.
  • NASA and NOAA data sources: Scientific observations and environmental measurements.
  • NASA POWER REST API: Live environmental data integration.

We also developed a centralised audio engine using React Context, allowing the application to maintain consistent playback state and coordinate audio generation with visualisations.

Creativity, Scientific Considerations and Innovation

The creative aspect of this project is the intersection of astrophysical-style data sonification techniques, environmental science, mathematics, music and interactive technology. We approached sound as an alternative scientific interface rather than a decorative addition to a dashboard.

An important engineering consideration was preserving the relationship between the original scientific measurement and the resulting sound. Different variables have different units, ranges and distributions. Therefore, we implemented validation, normalisation and configurable linear, logarithmic and exponential scaling before translating measurements into musical frequencies. This helps make datasets with substantially different numerical ranges suitable for auditory exploration.

We also considered temporal consistency, interpretability, playback control, responsiveness and the distinction between historical scientific records and live-accessible measurements. The interface was designed to make the experience approachable without removing the scientific context behind the data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Earth's environmental changes are often communicated through complex datasets that can be difficult for non-specialists to interpret. Our project introduces another way to experience those changes.

By translating environmental measurements into sound, we aim to:

  1. Make Earth science more engaging and accessible to students, educators and the general public.
  2. Introduce an alternative sensory approach to understanding climate change and environmental patterns.
  3. Demonstrate how sonification can complement conventional scientific visualisation.
  4. Explore opportunities for auditory accessibility for people who may face barriers when interpreting visual-only information.
  5. Encourage curiosity about Earth's interconnected environmental systems through interactive scientific exploration.

Ultimately, Earth Information Jukebox is an attempt to change the relationship between people and planetary data. We did not want people to simply read that Earth's temperature is rising or that atmospheric carbon dioxide is increasing. We wanted to create a way for them to experience the patterns behind those measurements.

Our vision is simple: Earth has always been communicating through data. We built a way to listen.

Project: https://earthjukebox.netlify.app/
